summary.headline: Tempsens H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.7% to INR255 crores, with EBITDA up 12% to INR55 crores and PAT up 18% to INR36 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 33.7% to INR255 crores, helped by the newly consolidated Tempsens Germany, Tempsens Polska and Tempsens Measurement and Control. EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% of total income from 25.2%, as employee cost (up 41%) and other expenses (up 37%) were front-loaded ahead of new capacity. Export revenue more than doubled to about 37% of product revenue, and IPO proceeds were used to cut borrowings to INR40.7 crores from INR77.9 crores. Management expects a stronger second half as new products and capacity ramp up, with margins recovering progressively.

financial_highlights.change: +18.1% YoY; includes one-time deferred tax credit of INR1.3 crores on IPO expense
+41% YoY; includes ESOP charge of INR1.1 crores
vs INR77.9 crores on 31 Mar 2026; debt-to-equity 0.06x from 0.15x

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash profit before working capital changes

segments.name: Temperature sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 57% to INR133 crores, now 53% of product revenue; organic growth about 25%, led by thermal power plants and CVD equipment OEMs. Fuel cell sensor dispatches began in the last two months.

segments.name: Electrical heating
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 44% to INR47 crores, driven by oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East. Standard lab and life science furnaces are ETL and CE approved; first supplies made in October, bulk dispatches from Q3.

segments.name: Specialised cables
segments.commentary: Revenue reached about INR74 crores in H1, recovering from a softer Q1; UL-certified high-temperature wire harness supplies to OEMs start in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue more than doubled to INR94 crores (about 37% of product revenue vs 25%); organic export growth about 45%. Domestic revenue grew about 12% to INR159 crores.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth for FY27 expected in line with the blended growth of the last 3 years; H1 is tracking ahead of that range, helped by consolidated entities.

Profitability expected to improve progressively in H2 as harness, furnace and OEM sensor supplies ramp; management expects consolidated margins to return to prior-year levels (Pratik's 24-25% run-rate framing accepted).
Finance cost benefit from debt repayment to show from Q3; management said at least 1% uplift to profitability.
Employee cost absorption expected over the next half, fully absorbed next year.
Working capital days expected to remain constant year on year.
Five capacity projects commissioning between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28, with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores at full utilisation (management stated this is potential, not guidance).
capex_capacity: H1 capex INR36.7 crores, of which INR26 crores was leasehold land for specialised cables expansion; INR5.9 crores plant and equipment; INR4.8 crores capital work in progress.
Brownfield 50,000 sq ft contact-sensor plant in Unit 1, due Q3 FY28, peak revenue potential INR120 crores.

New 50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 6 for mid-voltage heaters, due Q1 FY28, peak revenue potential INR200 crores; mid-voltage heater certification expected by Q4 FY27. Separately, about 25,000 sq ft added for large custom furnaces.
Unit 8 cable plant due Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores. JV with Victura to acquire an 80,000 sq ft facility, commencing by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

Capacity utilisation about 80%. Net IPO proceeds: INR7.5 crores earmarked for capex in electrical heating and cables and INR14.1 crores for general corporate purposes, both unutilised at 30 September.
demand_pricing: About 95% of business is make-to-order; traditional order book about 3-4 months, OEM visibility about 1-2 years.

OEM business expected to reach about 15% of revenue next year; fuel cell sensor orders reportedly cover almost a year. Confirmed OEM orders cited: fuel cell sensors, life science furnaces, exhaust heaters with Victura JV.
MRO business about 25% of revenue, expected to stay at that level.
Management said sensors and heaters carry higher gross margins than cables, without giving a split.

Management stated that raw material price swings are passed through in customer pricing; no current competition in specialised low-volume products, but Chinese competition expected as OEM volumes grow.
Mid-voltage heater TAM cited at about US$600-800 million; AdBlue heater prototype with a European company could be similar in size to the exhaust heater opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sharply in Q2, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 gross margin should be in line with FY26 (about 46%), with the H1 dip linked to lower-margin newly acquired entities and a high-margin defence order in H1 FY26. Gross margin is expected to moderate as heater and furnace dispatches grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue comes from MRO, and how do margins differ by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: MRO is about 25% of revenue and is expected to stay at that level. Margin split by segment was not disclosed; sensors and heaters have higher gross margins than cables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for employee cost to be absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee costs will be absorbed into revenue over the next half year, and fully absorbed next year for the current expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate interest cost after debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said at least a 1% uplift to profitability from lower finance cost; finance cost was INR2.5 crores in H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity utilisation is about 80%. Traditional order book is about 3-4 months and OEM visibility about 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue and profit come from Germany and Poland?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the acquired entities contributed incremental revenue of about INR25-26 crores and are profitable.

risks_watch: Gross margin dip in H1 (45.7% vs 46% full-year FY26, with the H1 FY26 base boosted by a large defence order); H2 margin recovery is management's expectation, not yet shown.
Employee cost (+41%) and other expenses (+37%) ahead of capacity; EBITDA growth of 12% lags revenue growth of 34%.
Middle East disruption affecting oil and gas demand and approvals; timing uncertain.
Ramp-up risk on new OEM programmes (fuel cell, life science furnaces, AdBlue heaters still at prototype) and mid-voltage heater certification by Q4 FY27.
Capacity commissioning dates from Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28; the INR500 crore peak revenue potential is not guidance.
Chinese competition expected as OEM volumes grow; inventory rose about INR28 crores to INR139 crores in H1.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on H2 ramp-ups and OEM pipeline, with clear numbers on debt reduction. Cautious on near-term margins, which management attributed to front-loaded cost and consolidation mix. Some answers were vague on quantification (TAM, segment margins, mid-voltage revenue share), which management declined or could not give.
key_quotes: We measure temperature, we generate heat, and we connect it.
What we make is engineered, make-to-order, made in India, supplied to the world.
So overall we'll be coming to the similar margin, but some of the entities also what we added were having higher manpower cost.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided in line with blended 3-year growth (H1 revenue +33.7% to INR255 crores, tracking ahead), with five capacity projects (~INR500 crores peak potential, Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28) and some confirmed OEM orders, though the capacity potential is stated as not guidance and the blended growth figure is not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% from 25.2% and gross margin is 45.7%, but management expects consolidated margins back to the 24-25% run-rate as employee cost is absorbed over the next half and finance cost falls (at least 1% profitability uplift from Q3).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Five projects are committed with dates: Victura JV facility (Q1 FY28 per growth read, commencing by Q4 FY27), Unit 6 mid-voltage heater plant (Q1 FY28), Unit 8 cable plant (Q2 FY28), Unit 1 contact-sensor plant (Q3 FY28), with ~INR500 crore peak revenue potential, though management says this is potential, not guidance.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue rose 33.7% to INR255 crores, organic export growth ~45%, temperature sensing organic ~25%, and capacity utilisation is about 80%, with OEM visibility of 1-2 years and OEM share expected to reach ~15% of revenue next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% and H1 capex was INR36.7 crores, with INR7.5 crores of IPO proceeds for electrical heating and cables capex still unutilised and about 25,000 sq ft added for large custom furnaces planned, so further capex announcements are probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of INR255 crores is tracking ahead of the FY27 growth range (in line with blended 3-year growth), but the range is not quantified and H2 depends on the ramp.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA grew only 12% against 34% revenue growth, employee cost is up 41%, the H2 margin recovery is not yet shown, and mid-voltage certification is due by Q4 FY27 with Middle East disruption affecting oil and gas demand.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bulk dispatches of standard furnaces start Q3 FY27, UL-certified wire harness supplies start Q3 FY27, fuel cell sensor dispatches began in last two months, and mid-voltage heater certification is expected by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: OEM business ramp (~15% of revenue next year)
rows.why: OEM expected to reach about 15% of revenue next year; fuel cell sensor orders cover almost a year and exhaust heater orders are confirmed with the Victura JV.

rows.label: Debt cut to INR40.7 crore from INR77.9 crore
rows.why: Borrowings fell INR37 crore in H1 using IPO proceeds, with D/E down to 0.06x from 0.15x, and finance cost benefit shows from Q3 with at least 1% profit uplift.

rows.label: Inventory build risk
rows.why: Inventory rose about INR28 crore to INR139 crore in H1, while management expects working capital days to stay constant year on year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 ramp, OEM pipeline and debt reduction, but cautious on near-term margins and vague on TAM, segment margins and mid-voltage revenue share; analysts pushed on gross margin recovery and the timing of employee cost absorption.
